name: Cabbage
perishability: Moderately perishable. 1–2 weeks at room temperature; weeks to months near 0 °C.
summary: A cheap, bulky winter vegetable from the eastern plains, with hill and southern plateau crops filling the summer and monsoon. It tolerates more heat than cauliflower and stores better, so its price swings are milder, but winter gluts still push farm prices to a rupee or two a kilo.

key_numbers.label: Production
key_numbers.note: approx., recent years; second only to China

global: India is the second-largest cabbage producer after China; almost all of it is eaten domestically.

rows.hubs: Jharkhand, Karnataka (Belagavi, Kolar), Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, UP, Haryana, Himachal, Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris)

belts.name: Bengal plains
belts.note: Biggest winter supply; ships to the East and North-East.

belts.name: Belagavi and Kolar
belts.note: Plateau crops through much of the year for southern cities.

belts.name: Nilgiris
belts.note: Hill cabbage year-round via Mettupalayam market.

belts.name: Himachal and Uttarakhand
belts.note: Summer and monsoon supply for North India.

seasons.name: Southern plateau
seasons.note: Two or more crops a year.

lean_season: July–October, when plains supply has stopped.

climate.v: Tolerates frost better than most vegetables; long cold spells can trigger bolting in some varieties.
Even moisture; heavy rain or irrigation after dry spells splits heads.
Fertile loam, pH 6.0–6.5; club root in acidic hill soils.

pests.name: Diamondback moth
pests.impact: Key pest of crucifers; widespread insecticide resistance.

pests.name: Club root
pests.impact: Serious in Nilgiris and Darjeeling hills.

postharvest.shelf_ambient: 1–2 weeks if kept cool and shaded.
postharvest.shelf_cold: 3–6 weeks (early types) to 3–4 months (late, dense types).
postharvest.respiration: Non-climacteric; sensitive to ethylene (yellowing, leaf drop).
practices: Harvested when heads are firm; a few wrapper leaves are left for protection.
Shipped loose or in mesh bags in open trucks; it travels well compared with leafy vegetables.
Shredded and salad-cut cabbage sells at roughly double the whole-head price per kg.

steps.what: Cut and loaded loose or in bags.
Auctioned by weight or by the truckload.
Sold per piece or per kg; a staple in restaurants and street food.

supply_chain.packaging: Loose in trucks or 25–40 kg mesh bags.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series.

varieties.name: Golden Acre, Pride of India, Copenhagen Market
Pusa Mukta, Pusa Ageti
varieties.note: IARI; black-rot resistant and heat-tolerant types.

trade.exports: Small, to Nepal, Bangladesh and the Gulf.

policy.what: No MSP; occasional state relief when winter prices collapse.

history.what: Farm prices of ₹1–3/kg in Bengal and Bihar; crops left in the field.

signals: Hill arrivals and Himachal monsoon weather (Jul–Sep).
Planting conditions in Bengal and Odisha (Sep–Oct).
business: Low value per kg makes freight the main cost; regional sourcing matters more than for most vegetables.
Good keeping quality suits food-service and cloud kitchens buying in bulk.
Shredded cabbage and coleslaw mixes are a simple value-add on quick commerce.
